historical_claims.anchor: Chandler Davis studied the rotation of eigenvectors under perturbation in 1963 and 1965, and the sine-theta theorem appears, with the tangent and double-angle theorems, among the four headline results of Section 2 of the 1970 paper by Davis and William Kahan, after their 1969 announcement.

Davis and Kahan assert that the constants in all four are best possible, attained by two-dimensional examples, and that when the perturbation depends linearly on a small parameter the four estimates agree to first order.

They state the theorem for infinite as well as finite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces, for every unitarily invariant norm, and, with the domain conditions and a bounded residual, for unbounded self-adjoint operators with half-infinite spectral intervals.
historical_claims.source_locator: Introduction; closing scope paragraphs of Section 2; Appendix to Section 6

related_resources.reason: The original paper; read Section 2 for the four headline theorems and Section 6 for the sine-theta proof.
First-order eigenvector perturbation, which the sine-theta theorem makes rigorous and non-asymptotic.
Chapter VII presents the Davis-Kahan sin theta theorem for matrices and related perturbation bounds.
Weyl's inequality is the usual way to certify the separation delta from an original eigengap and the size of the perturbation.
